title: Worn clothing and other worn textile articles

review.classification: The complete CPC 3.0 notes on PDF page 201 identify 39217. The garments are already worn and remain individual wearable shirts. The adjacent 39218 rag scope and 39214–39216 fibre wastes have different physical states. WCO HS 2022 Chapter 63 Note 3 independently confirms appreciable wear and bulk/bale/sack presentation for the trade category. Use market, cohort and item records to prove each in the selected bulk route.
review.primary_evidence: Pacific Clothing describes knit/woven sorting, a specifically identified short-sleeved cotton round-neck T-shirt stream, item-level reinspection against customer grades and packing for sale. Its film-and-strap bales do not establish these sacks or any cleaning or repair. The JRC sorting study and the Austrian preparation-for-reuse guide support selection by condition, checking suitability and documenting work. Enforce actual LDPE sack, receiving grade, need for treatment and transfer evidence. Use jurisdiction-specific legislation only where applicable.
review.measurement: One net first-release garment mass Q, with item grading, measured trim, contamination and moisture records. Transfers cancel between collection and preparation; packaging acquisitions, externally received sacks and returns of the same identified previously issued sacks are separate physical movements. Inspect inherited burdens and joint sort outputs on the actual route. Routine storage, reinspection, resale, returned garments and the number of future wears are separate from first release.
review.readiness: English and Chinese contain 26 atomic exchange cards each. The independently repeated PCR check performed 133 checks with zero skips, retaining 18 warnings for absent observed ranges. The manifest records 18 unresolved exchange identities, including the reference worn garment, actual provider selections and several auxiliary or waste exchanges. Methodology remains candidate/authored and scientific review, site evidence, reviewed translation and publication remain outstanding.
review.original_native_records: The pinned PE-LD foil and Liquid Detergent are Product flows referenced to Mass; each requires actual formulation/material and supply compatibility. The foil cannot bind discarded sack treatment. The archived water-vapour flow belongs to elementary emissions and does not represent retained garment moisture or wastewater. Energy refers to version 01.00.000 of the energy unit group, while the archived group is 03.00.003. The physically established MJ/kWh conversion provides meter support without selecting any electricity provider.
